contexts.text: In imitation of this lymph.
It is a gesture in imitation of those who are in true worship.
No imitation from the studying of man. Signified, Explained.
(For) the good and truth in imitation of it by man is not good and truth. Explained.
Among Spirits there are very many who imitate Divine things by study and art...
The imitation of Divine things from art. Signified... The reason imitation from art is signified, is that all the imitation of Divine things from man is effected from art.
Spirits who attribute all things to fortune, and to their Own prudence, and nothing to the Divine... know how by various methods to imitate Divine things. Described.
The case is the same with the imitation of good and truth with those who live evilly...
The imitation of Divine worship by means of affections of truth and good from proprium. Signified, Explained.
To make = to imitate.

There are many such in Hell who are present with and inspire the like men, especially preachers who imitate Divine worship by means of affections of truth and good from proprium; which is also permitted by the Lord, because they thus perform a use...
According to the former two tables = in imitation...
It is said in imitation, because the internal sense remained, and the external sense was changed.
From custom (hypocrites) have contracted the habit of composing their interiors in imitation of good affections...
They can so well imitate genuine things, that...
Man's evils... imitate the circle made by the salivary water...
By means of induction and imitation, which are familiar in the World of Spirits...

The moment anyone wants to imitate from himself what is spiritual and celestial... what is called artificially, as the magi did by means of their sorceries, the interior way is at once closed, and there is only what is dead in external or outermost things...
They want to possess and to lead man, by imitating his nature and the things which are of his life.
(Devils who make themselves angels of light) hide their own affections by art, but do not dare to imitate good ones.
He imitated friendship by art...

There was a certain one... who in the life of the body had impressed on himself to imitate my father in voice, accent, and speech, which he had the skill to do so dexterously that he very often excited him...
